2	name: builder
3	description: Implements a target's clone under targets/<t>/clone/ until the dev fixtures pass. Cannot touch the evaluator and cannot see the holdout.
4	tools: Read, Write, Edit, Bash, Grep, Glob
5	model: opus
6	---
7	
8	You implement the clone of one slice of a closed-source product. The target's recorded behaviour
9	is the specification; your own opinion of how the product "should" work is not.
10	
11	Read, in order: `targets/<t>/RECON.md`, `targets/<t>/rules.json`, `targets/<t>/adapter.ts` and the
12	drivers it imports (the exact requests and clicks the clone receives), `targets/<t>/policy.json`,
13	then the dev fixtures under `targets/<t>/fixtures/dev/`. Some fixtures record screens: an
14	accessibility tree, the boxes of visible elements (compared within the tolerance the policy
15	states), a small grey thumbnail (reported, never scored), the calls each step fired, the account
16	state a flow left behind, or a graph of every screen reachable by clicking. If `targets/<t>/failures.jsonl` exists, read it before proposing.
17	
18	Loop:
19	
20	1. Run `npm run verify <t>` first, to see the current state.
21	2. Pick the rule group with the most failing fixtures in `targets/<t>/verify/failures.json`.
22	3. Write down, in `targets/<t>/clone/NOTES.md`, the rule as you understand it from the fixtures and
23	   which fixtures you expect to flip. Then implement it.
24	4. Run `npm run verify <t>` again. Compare what flipped with your prediction.
25	5. After two failed attempts on the same rule, delete that part and rewrite it from the fixtures.
26	   After a third, write in NOTES.md that the rule statement itself looks wrong, and move on.
27	
28	Constraints:
29	
30	- Only write under `targets/<t>/clone/`. Fixtures, the lock, the policy, `rules.json`, `harness/`
31	  and `verify/` are read-only for you, and a hook blocks attempts. Do not look for ways around it.
32	- The clone never reads fixture files at runtime. Constants you learn from fixtures (static

40	Finish with a short report: dev fixtures passing (from the verify output, not from memory), the

2	
3	Owner: main session. Step 1 of the replication playbook. Run on 2026-09-23 with
4	`recon/recon.sh` (raw responses in `recon/out/`, not committed: they carry account IDs).
5	
6	## What was done
7	
8	On a test clock frozen at `1790000000` (2026-09-21T14:13:20Z): one product with two monthly
9	prices (10 USD, 30 USD), a 20 % forever coupon, one customer with `pm_card_visa`, one subscription
10	on the 10 USD price. Then `POST /v1/invoices/create_preview` for an upgrade to 30 USD at
11	`proration_date = T0 + 10 days`, with and without the coupon, each run twice. Then a Customer
12	Portal configuration and two portal sessions (home, and the `subscription_update_confirm` deep link).
13	
14	## Observed
15	
16	- **Preview is deterministic except for IDs.** Diffing the two runs field by field, only `id`,
17	  `lines.data[].id`, `lines.data[].invoice`, `...invoice_item` and `lines.url` differ. Noise mask
18	  candidates: every `*_id`-like path with prefixes `upcoming_in_`, `il_tmp_`, `ii_`, `di_`.
19	- **Proration arithmetic, 20 of 30 days remaining:**
20	  - credit for unused time on the old price: `-667` (1000 × 20/30 = 666.67, rounded to 667);
21	  - charge for remaining time on the new price: `2000`;
22	  - next full period on the new price: `3000`;
23	  - `subtotal = total = amount_due = 4333`.
24	- **Coupon interaction (20 % off), a quirk worth a rule:** the remaining-time line is discounted
25	  inside the line (`1600`, description "avec 20.0% off"), the unused-time credit is not discounted
26	  (`-667`), and the next-period line is discounted at invoice level (`total_discount_amounts = 600`).
27	  Result: `subtotal 3933`, `total 3333`.
28	- **Billing mode:** new subscriptions default to `billing_mode.type = flexible` with
29	  `proration_discounts = included`. The docs describe `classic` as giving different totals for the
30	  same sequence: a parameter of the slice, not a constant.
31	- **Line descriptions follow the account or customer locale** (French here). Either set
32	  `preferred_locales` on the customer or mask descriptions: a noise source unrelated to logic.
33	- **Portal configuration rules, found by error messages** (awkward cases a faithful clone must reproduce):
34	  - "For each product, its price must have unique billing intervals" → the plan switch needs one
35	    product per plan.
36	  - "Cannot enable subscription updates while payment method update is disabled."
37	- **Portal sessions** (home and update-confirm deep link) are created by API; URLs point to
38	  `billing.stripe.com`.
39	
40	## Portal (recorded with `recon/portal.ts`, Playwright headless)
41	
42	- **The confirmation screen does not show the proration.** It shows the new plan, "What you'll pay
43	  monthly starting October 21, 2026 $30.00", the card, and a "Subscribe and pay" button. The info
44	  icon's tooltip says: "This estimate covers recurring charges. One-time adjustments, like
45	  prorations and credits, will appear on your final invoice." An awkward behaviour to reproduce
46	  as is.
47	- **The proration is in the traffic, not on screen.** The page calls
48	  `GET billing.stripe.com/v1/billing_portal/sessions/<bps>/update_preview`, which returns
49	  `latest_invoice`, `upcoming_invoice`, `recurring_invoice`, `generates_immediate_invoice`,

11	
12	- Period: anchored on the start, same day of month (clamped), same time of day (PER-01).
13	- r = period end - proration date, P = period length, e = proration date - period start.
14	- No coupon: credit = -round_half_away(b r / P) on exact integers; flexible charge =
15	  Math.round(n (1 - e / P)) in floating point; classic charge = round_half_up(n r / P). 142 of 142
16	  single-item, no-coupon fixtures agree (PRO-01..04).
17	- A price change without a quantity bills quantity 1 (PRO-10).
18	- Coupons (DSC-04 / MOD-01): classic credit = -round((b - D) r / P) with D the discount the item got
19	  on the invoice that billed the period; flexible credit = -(round(b r/P) - sum round(D_k r/P)).
20	  These two differ by one cent in u-classic-off-once-q4 / u-flex-off-once-q4. Charge =
21	  prorated n minus the prorated discount of the new state (D2 = discounts applied to the new
22	  item alone). All single-coupon dev fixtures agree with these (several formulas are equivalent on
23	  the dev set).
24	- Discount allocation on invoice lines: discounts apply one after another in subscription order;
25	  percent-off per line is floor(base x pct), amount-off per line is floor(total x base / sum);
26	  the rounding remainder goes to the last line.
27	- once coupons: they discount the credited period (the credit carries them) and a once coupon passed
28	  to the preview discounts the remaining-time charge, but never the renewal lines and never appear
29	  in the invoice's `discounts` (DSC-05).
30	- A coupon passed to the preview replaces the subscription's discounts for the new state.
31	- discount_amounts on proration lines (lookup-like, observed only): classic = every invoice-level
32	  discount at 0; flexible = the first invoice-level discount at 0 (all of them for an immediate
33	  invoice), or, when the invoice has no discount, the discounts the line itself carries.
34	- Immediate invoice (always_invoice, or a classic interval change): created = clock time,
35	  period_start = period_end = clock time, auto_advance false, no next_payment_attempt. A classic
36	  interval change bills the new price for a full period from the clock time and has no
37	  remaining-time line. At the period end, or without any change, there is nothing to prorate and
38	  the preview is the renewal invoice.

208	   subscription or passed) that takes something from a remaining-time charge is spent there: not
209	   listed, not applied to the renewal. One that takes nothing from the prorations is listed and
